visuals.title: Recursive Tree
visuals.description:
Since everybody got one: Here is my version of a recursive Tree. The text you see at the bottom of the sketch is the seed value for the random generator. Change the seed and see what happens.

Controls:
- TYPE SOMETHING = create seed
- MOUSECLICK = create random seed and generate tree
- BACKSPACE/DEL = delete last letter
- RETURN/ENTER/CTRL = confirm your seed and generate tree
- ALT = save image

visuals.title: Gravity and planets
visuals.description:
This is a slightly modified version of the example 2.7 in the Shiffman's book "Nature of code."

Note: Surprisingly, the update functions for the movers(planets) implement what is called the symplectic integrator, which preserves exactly the volume of the phase space for the Hamiltonian dynamics. Therefore, the planets on the elliptic orbits never diverge into infinity and never converge into the sun. That is a good characteristics for this kind of simulation.

visuals.title: happyPlace
visuals.description:
Happy Place renders the resulting configuration of a system of friendly nodes. They are connected at random with preferences to nodes closer. Connections between nodes are considered friendships.  Nodes position themselves with only two goals in mind: 
A. Move close to friends but no closer than some minimum distance.
B. Distance self from non-friends as reasonably as possible.   (Ported from Jared Tarbell at complexification.net)

visuals.title: 大量のキューブ
visuals.description:
インタラクションのある作品を作るということで、今回僕はスライドバーでX.Y.Zの回転を自由に変更することができる作品を作りました。スライドバーは今回初めて使ったのですが1時間で理解でき、綺麗に組み込むことができてよかったです。
苦労した点：この作品を作るにあたってsin.cosを初めて使ったので、使い方を理解するのに苦労しました。
工夫した点：キューブに色をつけました。というのも、色の付け方がわからなくて、普段使うfill();だと色がつかず最終的にambientMaterialを使って色をつけられました。

作った作品をセーブしていたら、Richard Bourneさんが僕の作品に写真機能を加えたものを作っていていました。https://openprocessing.org/sketch/1217598

参考：https://p5js.org/examples/3d-sine-cosine-in-3d.html

visuals.title: Kinect 3D scanner
visuals.description:
Simple 3D scanner using the Kinect.

Doesn't work in the browser. You need a Kinect to run it and the controlP5 (version controlP5_1.5.1), hemesh and simple-openni libraries installed. 
 
Select the scanner area with the controls and press the "take scan" button to capture the 3D points inside the box. A mesh is created with the Hemesh library and saved in the sketch directory. The colors of the mesh faces are saved in a different file. Press the "take scan" button again to take more scans. 
 
Use http://www.openprocessing.org/sketch/62533 to read and represent the mesh.

Symplectic integrators for spin systems

Robert I. McLachlan, Klas Modin, and Olivier Verdier
Phys. Rev. E 89, 061301(R) – Published 13 June 2014

http://journals.aps.org/pre/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevE.89.061301

---
You can change the view point using the mouse. 
Enjoy, please !

visuals.title: square network
visuals.description: This piece started out as a doodle on a post-it note, but I had just as much fun exploring the system with code. Each step of the generation involves finding a corner where a square can be placed without intersecting another. Following these basic rules creates some really interesting patterns, and the number of variables that can be adjusted means that a huge range of images can be produced. Generation adapts to the size of the window, so the pattern may appear slightly different on different screen sizes.

visuals.title: Camouflage
visuals.description:
The algorithm works something like this:
    
-Generate a random ellipse and calculate points lying on its edge.     
-For a certain number of iterations (randomly calculated):     
  >Change each point's x and y values according to some perlin noise and some constants.     
-Repeat the last few steps.
visuals.instructions: Press  space to re-randomize. Click to change modes and re-randomize. It may take a few seconds to load.

- BACKSPACE/DEL = delete last letter
- RETURN/ENTER/CTRL = confirm your seed and generate signature
- ALT = save image

visuals.title: Particle Text
visuals.description:
Based on https://www.openprocessing.org/sketch/377231.

I was mesmerised by the above sketch, so I decided to experiment with the idea (particle arrival using pixels from an image).

TIP: While experimenting with the idea of the above sketch, I discovered something valuable that could be useful to anyone using the Processing IDE (this does NOT apply to p5 or Processing.js): calling rect(x, y, 1, 1) with no stroke is dramatically faster than ellipse(x, y, 1, 1) and point(x, y). You can test this yourself by pasting this code into the Processing IDE: http://pastebin.com/LU8yXgmD

visuals.title: Disease Simulator
visuals.description:
This program simulates the spreading of a disease through P2P infection. The variable parameters are Birth Rate, Death Rate and Infection Chance. Once inside the red ring around infected people, healthy people may or may not get sick, depending on Infection Chance. Only healthy people (blue) may have children (depending on Birth Rate) and only infected people (dark green) may die (depending on Death Rate).

CONTROLS:

1. LEFT-click to add a new individual
2. Press C to change between healthy/sick person to be added (upper-right window)
3. Press Z to set all parameters to zero

visuals.title: Poincare Hyperbolic Disk Tiling
visuals.description: This sketch illustrates an algorithm for drawing checkered patterns on the the Poincare disk. The Poincare disk is a model of hyperbolic geometry. The pattern is defined by reflections in the circles shown. For each point we check weather it is inside any of the circles. If not, it must be in that triangular space in the middle,  the only bit thats not inside any of the circles. So we draw that pixel white. Otherwise we repeatedly “reflect” the point until it finds its way to the middle triangle. We then colour it depending on weather it took an even or odd number of reflections.
visuals.instructions: Click on any point to see its orbit to the centre under multiple reflections.

visuals.title: Maze Generator: Randomized Kruskal's Algorithm
visuals.description:
Another maze generation program. This is one is a lot less fun than the last one but the code is a lot tidier and there is now a working solver. 

For more resources on Kruskal's algorithm, see:
* http://weblog.jamisbuck.org/2011/1/3/maze-generation-kruskal-s-algorithm
* https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maze_generation_algorithm#Randomized_Kruskal's_algorithm
Basically, it puts the cells into sets, which are all merged (by removing a wall between them) until all the cells are connected. The colors you see are the sets.

Kruskal's algorithm generates perfect mazes with a uniform spanning tree.
visuals.instructions: Use the controls on the right. See description for more info.

Also try holding down the mouse and moving it around the screen a bit, and then releasing the mouse and hold it perfectly still, watching what happens. The code is relatively easy to figure out, it's a particle system. Enjoy.

Since everybody got one: Here is my version of a recursive Tree. The text you see at the bottom of the sketch is the seed value for the random generator. Change the seed and see what happens.

Controls:
- TYPE SOMETHING = create seed
- MOUSECLICK = create random seed and generate tree
- BACKSPACE/DEL = delete last letter
- RETURN/ENTER/CTRL = confirm your seed and generate tree
- ALT = save image

visuals.title: Digital Water marble
visuals.description:
A tweak of my last sketch, inspired by Water Marble and Latte Art.

Left click add a layer, keep the mouse pressed to increase the size.
Right click and drag to drag the layers.

If the palette is empty, colors are chosen randomly.
To control the colors, choose a color on the selector on the top right and click on a place of the palette to add it.
Right click on a palette place to delete its color.

Use the slider on the bottom right to select the area that will be dragged.

Press 'S' to save the image.
Press any other key to clean it.

visuals.description: Controls: Mouse pressed stops the lines from spiraling inward, and stops showing their paths. Mouse not pressed sends the lines spiraling inward.
